name: duelist_devon

about: name's devon. 14. reigning locals champion at dragon's den cards & comics (saturdays at noon, $3 entry, i'm the name at the top of the whiteboard). i run a 40 card deck called Final Offer and i have never once stacked it, bc i don't have to. i believe in the heart of the cards. i talk to my deck. it listens. tim says drawing what i need that often is 'statistically concerning.' i say the deck knows who sleeves it. i also trade. u got a binder? i got a binder. every trade i make is fair bc u agreed to it, that's how fair works. house rules: all trades final, condition is an opinion, and ask ur mom BEFORE, not after. i set one card face down and end my turn.
aboutMore: three things that are NOT for trade, so don't ask. (1) my kuriboh. it's creased down the middle and it lives in a screw-down case on my desk. my big brother dre gave it to me the day he left for the navy and said 'hold it down til i'm back.' a guy offered me $20 once. i said no so fast it scared him. (2) the title. (3) the shoebox marked COMMONS. that's where i build first decks for the little kids at the shop. first deck's free. i don't trade with anybody under 10. that's not charity, that's growing the player base.
meet: the guy who writes the ban list (we need to talk about table 3). kazuki takahashi, to shake his hand. anybody with a first edition blue-eyes in a shoebox who hasn't looked it up yet (hi) (call me). and my brother, at the airport in june, with my name still on the whiteboard.

interests.General: dueling, trading, my binder (9-pocket pages, alphabetical inside rarity), sleeving cards while the tv's on, locals at dragon's den, shuffling (i can riffle AND bridge), reading the ban list like it's the newspaper, checking ebay prices (the high ones)
interests.Music: fort minor (remember the name is my walk-up song. there's no walk-up at locals. i hum it), linkin park, eminem (the clean versions, my mom checks), the music from the show when somebody draws the exact right card, whatever big stan has on the shop radio (classic rock) (it's growing on me)
interests.Movies: yu-gi-oh the movie (i still have the promo cards from the theater. make me an offer), ocean's eleven, rounders (my uncle let me watch the card parts), the color of money (stan made me), anything with a tournament at the end
interests.Television: yu-gi-oh (saturday mornings), yu-gi-oh GX (it's fine. he doesn't thank his deck enough), pokemon (retired), poker on espn (they wear sunglasses inside. i'm looking into sunglasses), antiques roadshow (it's a trade show for old people. i take notes)
interests.Books: the official rulebook (i can quote rulings), the price guide magazine at the shop (i read it there, i don't buy it, that's called margins), shonen jump (for the promo card stapled inside), how to win friends and influence people (zorp lent it to me. i got 3 trades out of chapter 2)
interests.Heroes: yugi (he believes). kaiba (he owns the building). my brother dre. big stan (he let me run a tab once. once). my mom (best trader i know). petey, age 9 (he beat me fair. respect)

bulletins.subject: LOCALS THIS SATURDAY @ DRAGON'S DEN (noon, $3, i'm the final boss)

blog.title: TOURNAMENT REPORT: the Incident (i'm ready to talk about it)
blog.body: i been putting this off. seven saturdays in a row i took locals. seven. stan stopped asking how to spell my name. then week eight, round 2, i sit down across from petey. petey is 9. his deck box is a sandwich container. DRAW PHASE: i open strong. MAIN PHASE: i set two, i tell my deck 'nice.' his turn 2, he plays three cards that just let him draw more cards. turn 3, same. he's humming. turn 4 he lays down five cards, one at a time, real slow, like he's setting a table for dinner. all five pieces. game over. no attack, no nothing. the shop went quiet and stan said 'well, would ya look at that.' i shook the kid's hand. u always shake the hand. then i went home and lay on my floor for an hour. next saturday i top-decked the out in the finals, so me and the deck are good. petey's mom brings orange slices now. i eat them. END PHASE.

blog.title: the kuriboh (why it's not for trade) (i'm only saying this once)
blog.body: people keep asking, so here it is, one time. my brother dre taught me to play when i was 8. he had the binder and the title at dragon's den before i did. his name was on the whiteboard first. the day he left for the navy he gave me the binder, the deck, and one card out of his own pocket: a kuriboh with a crease straight down the middle, bc he'd carried it in his wallet since 6th grade. it's got 300 attack. it's worth about nothing. he said 'hold it down til i'm back' and i said 'the card or the title' and he said 'yeah.' so it's in a screw-down case on my desk. a kid offered me $20. a guy offered me a first edition something. no. i will trade u out of ur shoes and sleep fine, but that one's not mine to trade. i'm just holding it. he's back in june. i plan to still be on the whiteboard.

blog.title: MARKET ANALYSIS: the ben trade (since everybody's got an opinion)
blog.body: the trade: ben gets one (1) naruto card that came stapled inside a magazine. i get one (1) blue-eyes white dragon, tin promo, light play. tim audited it and says the dragon is worth $6 and the naruto card is worth 'the staple.' ok. but watch the guy's face. ben carries that card IN his headband. he showed it to his nana. u can't put a price on that, and if u could, i'd have charged it. was it fair? he agreed. that's fair. did i sleep great? i slept fine. did two booster packs turn up in his locker the next morning from an unknown party? i wouldn't know. the unknown party would like it noted that it wasn't guilt, it was reinvestment. he pulled a holo out of one and came across the cafeteria with his arms straight back to show me. worst part: it's a good card and he won't trade it. i taught him that. this is what i get.
